Tour.Title: Mystery Engine: Keeper Tour
Tour.Description: A guided tour of the system for the Keeper: compendiums, character sheets and the notebook.
Tour.WelcomeContent: This system runs games carved from Brindlewood Bay — Brindlewood Bay itself, The Between, Public Access and anything built along the same lines. This short tour shows the pieces you need as a Keeper. You can leave it at any time and restart it later from Tour Management in the settings.
Tour.ConceptTitle: Sheets are built, not filled in
Tour.ConceptContent: The system knows none of these games. A character sheet starts empty and you assemble it: abilities and labels are plain data, everything else — moves, checklists, questions — are items on the actor. That is what makes one system able to run all of them.
Tour.CompendiumsContent: Everything ready-made lives here. Playbooks holds complete character sheets, Items the move collections you pick from, and Documentation a journal with the details behind this tour.
Tour.PlaybooksContent: The Playbooks compendium is sorted into one folder per game: The Between with its seven playbooks, Public Access with the Latchkey, Brindlewood Bay with the Murder Maven. Drag one into the actors directory and the whole sheet comes with it — moves, checklists, abilities and the XP track of that game.
Tour.SheetContent: This is a playbook in play mode. The header carries the labels of the game (Look, Vice, Style …), the abilities and the XP track. Everything below it is items.
Tour.AbilitiesContent: Click an ability to open the roll dialog: a plain roll of 2d6, or 3d6 keeping the best or worst two for advantage and disadvantage. The result lands in chat with its outcome band — 12+, 10+, 7-9 or a miss.
Tour.ManualRollContent: The die next to the abilities opens the same dialog for a free roll, where you type the modifier yourself.
Tour.ConditionsContent: Conditions are free text and can be added straight from play mode. There is no fixed list — write what the fiction calls for.
Tour.MovesContent: A move card shows the fiction first and the rules below it. Roll outcomes are rendered as coloured badges so the line you need at the table is easy to find.
Tour.MoveActiveContent: Every move of the playbook is on the sheet from the start; the optional ones are greyed out. Tick the checkbox in the card header to activate the move a player picked — and untick it if they change their mind. The eye next to it hides a move entirely, which can only be undone in edit mode.
Tour.ChecklistsContent: Checklists cover everything that gets marked off: Dawn Questions, Advancements, the Masks or Crowns. Some are containers with writable lines instead — Personal Quarters, Your Corner of the House, A Cozy Little Place.
Tour.EditToggleContent: The lock in the window bar switches the sheet between play and build mode. The icon always shows the mode you are in, the tooltip the one you are switching to.
Tour.EditModeContent: In build mode you add abilities and labels, create moves and checklists, sort them and set which ones are active or hidden. This is where you assemble a playbook of your own — or adjust a ready-made one.
Tour.MarkupContent: Two kinds of markup: descriptions are rich text, checklist entries take bbCode such as [b]bold[/b]. Roll outcomes are written as [ON 10+], [ON 7-9], [ON hit] or [ON miss] at the start of a line and become coloured badges — that works in any language.
Tour.NotebookIconContent: This icon opens the notebook, the Keeper's board for the mystery in play. CTRL+J works as well.
Tour.NotebookContent: The notebook belongs to the active scene. If a scene has none yet, it offers to create one; an existing notebook item can be dropped onto the window instead. Switching scenes switches the notebook with it.
Tour.NotebookTabsContent: Actors shows the Hunters and their active moves at a glance — drop an actor onto the window to add them. Threats tracks questions, clues and countdowns, and each of them can be hidden from the players. Pages is free notes.
Tour.ThreatsContent: Threats have their own actor type. They are built exactly like a character sheet — items, no fixed structure — and give you a place for the moves and lists a threat brings to the table.
Tour.DocumentationContent: The Documentation compendium has the written version of all this, including the markup reference. Restart this tour any time from Tour Management in the settings. Have a good mystery!
